title: fix(spec): flip `field.relatedListFilter` to `live` — its flip condition landed at the objectui pin
body:
Fixes #19187

Clause-②: no

`packages/spec/liveness/field.json` recorded `field.relatedListFilter` as `status: planned` + `authorWarn: true`, so `packages/lint`'s ledger-driven advisory repeated the row's own `authorHint` at every compile — 「the auto-derived related list does not apply this filter yet」 — about a key the **pinned** console applies. A true warning costs an author nothing; a false one steers them off a usable key.

The row wrote its own flip condition, and the condition had already been met.

## First leg — the defect is still there (re-taken, not inherited)

Reproduced independently on fetched `origin/main` @ `7d0f911da9`:

```
packages/spec/liveness/field.json -> .props.relatedListFilter   status=planned  authorWarn=true
LIT CONTROL, same walk, same file: 87 ledger entries (top level + drilled children)
                                   carry a `status`  =>  the instrument reads this
                                   file, so the hit is a reading and not a missed search
```

The lit control reads non-zero, so the round stands. It also reconciles exactly with the dispatching seat's 87. One reading worth recording so the next walk does not re-derive it: **87 is entries-including-`children`**; a top-level-only walk of the same file reads **67**, and `check-liveness.mts`'s own walked shape for this type reads **93** (it counts the ADR-0010 protection envelope, which is not a ledger row). Three correct numbers for three different denominators.

## Second leg — the flip condition, re-measured rather than relayed

The card relayed three readings from another seat. Every one was re-run here, and one of them was relayed at the wrong tree.

| Reading | Result |
|---|---|
| Today's `.objectui-sha` on `origin/main` | `53ded82bf7a494f54e344e19099dbf00854b8694` — read here, not taken on faith |
| `deriveRelatedLists` reads `fieldDef.relatedListFilter` | yes — **at the pin, lines 276-277**, not 301-302 |
| Shipped with objectui `d796c8dde` | yes — `feat(detail): derived related lists consume the FK's relatedListFilter` (objectui PR #6946, 2026-08-31) |
| `git merge-base --is-ancestor d796c8dde 53ded82bf7` | **exit 0** |

⚠️ **The relayed line numbers were measured on objectui `main`, not at the pin.** `deriveRelatedLists.ts:301-302` is correct at objectui HEAD `dda8f3815d` and is 25 lines off at `53ded82bf7`, which is the tree this repo actually builds against. The ledger pointer this PR writes cites the pin. That is the #10068 discipline — read both pointers at the pin, never at objectui main — and it is the reason the re-run was owed.

**Shallow-clone control.** The objectui checkout in this session **is shallow** (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` -> `true`, depth 50, one graft at `19424d67ef`). The ancestor reading is unaffected and a control leg was run anyway rather than resting on the instrument note:

- the ancestry path is fully materialized in this object store — `git rev-list --ancestry-path d796c8dde..53ded82bf7` returns **293** commits, so the exit 0 walked a real chain rather than being handed one;
- **control leg at greater depth**: `d796c8dde^` (`836e97971b`, strictly deeper than the commit under test) `--is-ancestor 53ded82bf7` -> **exit 0**. A truncation that could hide ancestry would have answered exit 1 here first.

A shallow clone can only *hide* ancestry, never invent it, so the exit 0 is self-attesting; the control leg is recorded because the reading is load-bearing and the check was cheap. The repo was left shallow — nothing needed unshallowing.

## The evidence pointer

The row now carries the ledger's own cross-repo convention, matched to its three `relatedList*` siblings (`evidenceScope: cross-repo`, realm-marked paths, symbol anchors, a pinned foreign commit) rather than a new field:

- `objectui: packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts#deriveRelatedLists:276` puts the authored value on the derived descriptor as `filter`, gated by the same file's `#isDeclaredFilter` predicate — the declared-vs-absent discrimination its `relatedListTitle` / `relatedListColumns` siblings do;
- `objectui: packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx#synthParts:2079` destructures that descriptor key as `declaredFilter` (`:2041`) and writes it onto the synthesized `record:related_list` node, so `RelatedList` AND-composes it with `{ [referenceField]: parentId }` and the tab strip's count probe composes the same pair;
- measured objectui `@53ded82bf7`, this repo's `.objectui-sha` pin.

`verifiedAt: 2026-09-20`. No `producer` field: the author IS the producer here (the consumer reads the authored value directly), same as the three siblings. No ADR-0054 `proof`: `proof-registry.mts` binds `field.type` and `field.readonly` only.

## Consequences followed, in this repo only

**The lint needed no code change** — `shouldWarn` is ledger-driven (`entry.authorWarn === true || entry.status === 'experimental'`), so dropping `authorWarn` is what stops the false sentence. What did need work is the two pins that used this key as their witness.

`field.relatedListFilter` was the **only** `authorWarn` row on `field.json` at any depth, so the flip empties `loadWarnMap(dir, 'field')` and `lintLivenessProperties` now skips the field walk entirely on its `if (fieldWarn.size > 0)` guard.

1. **`REAL LEDGER: field.relatedListFilter (planned)`** could no longer pin a verdict. Replaced with the disposition #6774 and #10068 used for exactly this shape: a **silence pin** (authored on `fields[1]`, and again across three fields, so a half-reverted flip — ledger back to `planned`, or the objectui pin rolled back under it — surfaces right there) plus an **anti-vacuity guard** that authors the flipped key and `object.externalSharingModel` in the same call, so "one warning and not two" distinguishes a real verdict from a lint whose ledger DIRECTORY did not resolve. The `planned` branch stays a contract test on `translation.flows` and `object.externalSharingModel`.
2. **The #11385 field-walk case** keeps its fixture and narrows its claim to the half still reachable — no throw, and the object walk still reaches its own finding past a malformed `fields` array. The "kept walking past the null FIELD" half is **not** asserted, because over a loop that no longer runs it would pass vacuously: the shape #7079 was filed to avoid writing. See the out-of-scope note below.

Two dated enumerations naming the key are corrected in place rather than left to read as current.

**Generated artefacts** were regenerated with the repo's own tooling, never hand-edited: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:liveness-counts` moved `field` from `live 90 / planned 2` to `live 91 / planned 1` and the totals with it. `check:liveness`'s own instruction to re-read the README Notes cell beside a moved count was followed: that cell describes the *dead* set, which this change does not touch, so it was not falsified — the flip is recorded there as the `view`/`app` rows record theirs.

## Reverse verification — the new pins can fail

Run from the committed state, mutation proven on disk, both legs recorded:

```
mutation   scripts/ablation-replace.mjs: anchor 1 -> 0, blob 7aa378b626aa -> b5396314b1f2
           (ledger row restored to `planned` + `authorWarn`; the lint resolves the ledger
           from the workspace package dir, so no dist hop is involved)
ablated    pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/lint-liveness-properties.test.ts
           -> 4 failed | 67 passed   (all four new/narrowed assertions red)
restore    git checkout HEAD -- THE.PATH;  worktree blob 7aa378b626aa == HEAD blob 7aa378b626aa,
           `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty
```

Direction observed: turns red, the common direction. Nothing about it is left behind — no permanent test file, and the restore is proven by blob identity rather than by an exit code.

## Checks — real exit codes

| Command | Exit |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:liveness` | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` | **0** — all 16 generated artefacts up to date |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:empty-state` | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:strictness-ledger` | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` | **0** — 105 files, 3976 passed, 5 skipped |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run` (liveness script suites + `src/data/field.test.ts`) | **0** — 5 files, 397 passed |
| `pnpm check:nul-bytes` · `check:merge-driver` · `check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `check:test-source-alias` · `check:published-files` | **0** each |
| `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` · `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main` · `check-changeset-fixed` | **0** each |

**eslint, as a declared narrowing rather than a repo scan.** `node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js .` over the repo root is the configured corpus; this run passed the five changed paths explicitly and read **5 files** back from `--format json`, exit **0**, **0 errors**. Four of the five report `File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied` — the JSON, the two Markdown ledgers and the changeset are outside the config's matched set — so the genuinely linted surface of this diff is the one TypeScript file, clean. The narrowing excludes nothing: `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting for ANY file (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules — stated and positive-controlled at `eslint.config.mjs:324-334`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on a file it does not touch. The repo-wide sweep is CI's.

All numbers above were taken at `HEAD` = the last commit on this branch; heavy runs went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` and each verdict is that wrapper's own `VERDICT command-exit` line, captured before any pipe.

## Merge-driver hygiene

`git check-attr merge --` was read **per file**, never counted off `.gitattributes`: `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts.md` is `merge: os-regen`; the other four paths are `unspecified`. `origin/main` had not moved from the branch point (`git rev-list --count 7d0f911da9..origin/main` -> 0), so no sync was performed — no rebase, no force-push, and `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` was not needed.

The diff was measured the stated way: `git add -A` first, then `git diff --cached`, with index blob hashes compared against the worktree files.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope for this card, measured here, not filed by this seat and not fixed in this PR:

- **The #11385 field-walk guard is now unreachable.** With zero warned rows on `field.json`, `if (fieldWarn.size > 0)` gates the whole field loop off, so `if (!isRecord(field)) continue` — the guard that case exists for — cannot be exercised through `lintLivenessProperties` at all, and there is no other warned field row to re-subject to (the field walk reads `field.json` and nothing else). This is the third time a correct flip has emptied a pin in this file (`dashboard.widgets.colorVariant` -> #7079, and the `app.navigation.runAction` fan-out block in this same test file), and that block's own recommendation applies unchanged: drive the nesting walk from a synthetic warn map through a package-internal seam, as `checkItemAgainstWarnMap` already does for `checkItem`, and leave the ledger-driven coupling to the assertions that are genuinely about the ledger. Not done here because it adds test-seam surface to `packages/lint` that this card did not authorize.
- **A stale pointer in `packages/spec/liveness/README.md:548`.** The `authorWarn` section names the lint as `packages/cli/src/utils/lint-liveness-properties.ts`; that path does not exist. The rule lives at `packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts` (lit control: that path resolves, and it is the module every assertion in this PR drives). A reader following the README lands nowhere.
- **Noted, not filed:** the relayed `deriveRelatedLists.ts:301-302` citation is correct on objectui `main` and wrong at the pin, which is the line-rot direction the ledger README already documents at length — handled inside this PR by citing the pin, with no separate carrier. Successor for the README note: none identified.

## ⚠️ Seat correction to this body — made AFTER delivery, named here rather than made silently

The `domain:spec` seat edited **two sentences** in this body after the round-2 fixes landed on head `f091bc16ae`. The delivered wording is quoted so nothing is laundered:

1. **The F2 overstatement, one artefact over.** This body said the anti-vacuity guard distinguishes a real verdict 「from a lint that **stopped loading ledgers**」. Narrowed to 「from a lint whose ledger **DIRECTORY** did not resolve」, because that is what it actually guards: removing `field.json` ALONE leaves the suite green (71 passed, exit 0) — `loadWarnMap` returns an empty map silently at `:77` and `:81-83`, and the guard's second warning comes from `object.json`, a separate load. The at-tier review raised F2 on exactly the principle that a sentence must say what it guards; leaving it here would have reproduced the finding in the document a reviewer opens first.
2. **A dangling issue number.** This body cited `#10262` twice. Measured: `#10262` answers **HTTP 404 in BOTH** `objectstack-ai/objectstack` and `objectstack-ai/objectui`; lit control, same instrument same act, `#7079` answers **200 in both**. The two citations are replaced by a description of the block. ⛔ The **nine pre-existing** `#10262` citations inside `lint-liveness-properties.test.ts` are left exactly as found — they predate this card.

⛔ Nothing else in this body was touched: the closing-keyword line and the `Clause-②: no` line — the body's only mechanical readers — are unchanged and were already correct. ⛔ The diff, the changeset and the labels were not touched by this edit.
